title: Manage a local service
goal: Distinguish service state, its process and its recent journal events.
challenge: Inspect the stopped ll-lifecycle.service, start it, identify the real service user/PID, restart it, then stop it cleanly. Explain active state versus enabled-at-boot state.

steps.command: systemctl status ll-lifecycle.service --no-pager; systemctl is-enabled ll-lifecycle.service
steps.explanation: A status command may return nonzero for a stopped service; that is an observation.
steps.expected: The prepared service is inactive and disabled.

steps.command: sudo systemctl start ll-lifecycle.service; systemctl show ll-lifecycle.service -p ActiveState -p MainPID -p User -p MemoryMax -p TasksMax
steps.explanation: Start the bounded service and inspect its current actual PID; no fixed PID is assumed.
steps.expected: ActiveState=active, a nonzero MainPID and User=ll-service.

steps.command: pid=$(systemctl show ll-lifecycle.service -p MainPID --value); ps -o pid,user,stat,args -p "$pid"
steps.explanation: Only inspect the currently reported PID. If the 120-second limit already expired, inspect the journal and restart the lab unit.
steps.expected: An ll-service process; not a root worker.

steps.command: sudo systemctl restart ll-lifecycle.service; sudo journalctl -u ll-lifecycle.service -n 12 --no-pager
steps.explanation: Restart replaces the invocation. Read timestamped LAB_READY and stop/start events.
steps.expected: A new invocation/PID is possible; no exact number is required.

steps.command: sudo systemctl stop ll-lifecycle.service; systemctl is-active ll-lifecycle.service
steps.explanation: Stop targets the entire named unit, avoiding broad process termination.
steps.expected: inactive; nonzero is-active status is expected.

hints: Use systemctl show for the current MainPID; never copy a PID from a lesson.
status, enabled state and journal answer different questions.
The timer bounds unattended practice; inspect its expiry instead of hiding it.
review: I matched the process to its unprivileged service user.
I observed start/restart/stop and explained disabled versus inactive.
coverage: Partial LPIC-2 202.1 systemd service management. Guest-only administration; completion records self-review, not verified assessment. No score.
